description: Set up the environment and perform runtime verification of the running app to gather the raw evidence the QA audit report will be built from. Install dependencies, confirm the project builds and lints cleanly, run the app, and use browser automation to capture responsive screenshots, console logs, and network behavior, plus HTTP header inspection. This feature produces evidence/artifacts only; the written report is FEAT-002.
steps: Prepend the working npm to PATH for every shell command: export PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" (npm is NOT on the default PATH; node is v22.23.3). Work inside /projects/sandbox/kiro-web-playground.
Install dependencies: npm install. node_modules is currently missing. Network is OPEN_INTERNET and the npm registry was verified reachable.
Run npm run build and capture full output. Record whether it succeeds, any warnings, and build timing. Save output to .agents/tasks/task-qa-audit/evidence/build.log.
Run npm run lint and capture full output to .agents/tasks/task-qa-audit/evidence/lint.log. Record warnings/errors (note eslint-config-next core-web-vitals + typescript rules are in effect).
Start the dev server in the background: npm run dev (http://localhost:3000). Wait until it is ready. (Alternatively build then npm run start.)

Use a browser-automation power to drive the running app. Activate it via kiro_powers action=activate powerName="playwright" (fall back to agent-browser if playwright is unavailable). Chromium is at /opt/playwright.

Load http://localhost:3000 at three viewport widths and capture a screenshot of each into /projects/sandbox/kiro-web-playground/qa-screenshots/: mobile (375x667), tablet (768x1024), desktop (1440x900). Also capture one dark-mode screenshot by emulating prefers-color-scheme: dark if the tooling supports it.

While the page is loaded, collect browser console messages (errors + warnings) and the network request list (status codes, any 404/500/failed/CORS). Save a summary to .agents/tasks/task-qa-audit/evidence/runtime.md. Specifically verify whether /favicon.ico and the SVG assets load, and whether any hydration or Next.js dev warnings appear.

Exercise interactive behavior that exists: keyboard Tab through the page to record focus order and whether visible focus indicators appear on the two text links and two CTA anchors; confirm the two CTA anchors open external URLs with target=_blank rel=noopener noreferrer, and that the two in-paragraph text links (Templates, Learning) do NOT have target/rel. Note window-resize/layout-shift behavior.

Inspect HTTP response headers: curl -I http://localhost:3000 and curl -I http://localhost:3000/next.svg. Record presence/absence of security headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy) into the evidence. Save to .agents/tasks/task-qa-audit/evidence/headers.log.
Stop the dev server when evidence collection is complete.

Write a concise evidence index at .agents/tasks/task-qa-audit/evidence/README.md listing every artifact produced and a one-line summary of each key finding, and record the same summary plus the exact build/lint/runtime results in this feature's findings field.
acceptance_criteria: npm install completes and node_modules exists.
npm run build result (success/failure + any warnings) is captured in evidence/build.log and summarized in findings.
npm run lint result is captured in evidence/lint.log and summarized in findings.
At least three responsive screenshots (mobile 375, tablet 768, desktop 1440) exist under /projects/sandbox/kiro-web-playground/qa-screenshots/.

Browser console output and network request statuses are recorded in evidence/runtime.md, explicitly noting any JS errors, warnings, 404s, 500s, failed assets, or CORS issues (or stating none were observed).
HTTP response headers for the document and a static asset are captured in evidence/headers.log with explicit notes on which security headers are present vs absent.
An evidence index README.md exists and this feature's findings field summarizes build, lint, console, network, header, and focus/keyboard observations with concrete values.
verification: cd /projects/sandbox/kiro-web-playground && export PATH="/root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin:$PATH" && npm run build (confirm the exit status recorded matches the evidence log)
Confirm the screenshot files and evidence/*.log|*.md files exist on disk.
findings:
ENVIRONMENT: node v22.23.3, npm v11.4.2 (PATH-prepended from /root/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.3/bin). `npm install` completed, added 427 packages; node_modules present. npm audit reported 15 vulnerabilities (1 low, 2 moderate, 11 high, 1 critical) in the dependency tree (informational, not blocking). Note on tooling: background processes do NOT survive across separate tool calls in this sandbox, so a persistent dev server could not be shared with the kiro_powers browser tools; instead each server-dependent step (curl headers; browser capture) ran inside a single bash call that starts `next start`, does the work, then stops it. Browser automation used playwright-core 1.63.0 (installed with --no-save) driving the system Chromium at /opt/playwright/chromium-1232/chrome-linux64/chrome with --no-sandbox.

BUILD (evidence/build.log): SUCCESS, exit 0. Next.js 16.2.4 (Turbopack). Compiled in ~1509ms, TypeScript OK in ~1390ms, 4 static pages generated in ~275ms, wall time ~4.4s. NO warnings. Routes: `/` and `/_not-found`, both prerendered static (○). This Next.js version's build output does NOT print per-route First Load JS byte sizes (size column omitted).

LINT (evidence/lint.log): PASS, exit 0. `eslint` (eslint-config-next core-web-vitals + typescript) produced zero errors and zero warnings. Build+lint re-run for verification both returned exit 0, matching the logs.

CONSOLE (evidence/runtime.md + runtime.json): ZERO console messages (0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 logs) and ZERO uncaught page errors on all three light viewports and in dark mode. No hydration warnings. Production server used so no dev-overlay/HMR noise.

NETWORK (evidence/runtime.md + runtime.json): EVERY request returned HTTP 200; no 404/500/failed/CORS. ~14 requests per load: document `/`, 1 CSS chunk, ~8 JS chunks (incl. Turbopack runtime), 2 self-hosted next/font Geist .woff2 files, /next.svg, /vercel.svg, and favicon.ico (served with a cache-busting query). favicon and both SVGs confirmed loading. All requests same-origin; no third-party/CDN runtime dependency.

HEADERS (evidence/headers.log): `/`, `/next.svg`, `/favicon.ico` all returned 200. ALL SIX security headers ABSENT on the document: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. `X-Powered-By: Next.js` IS present (framework info-disclosure). next.config.ts defines no headers(). Caching: document s-maxage=31536000 (prerendered static); /next.svg public,max-age=0; favicon public,max-age=0,must-revalidate.

KEYBOARD / FOCUS (evidence/runtime.json focusOrder+anchors): Tab order is logical source order — 1) Templates text link, 2) Learning text link, 3) Deploy Now CTA, 4) Documentation CTA, then focus leaves the page. VISIBLE focus indicator present on all four links (browser default outline-style:auto, outline-width:1px; nothing suppresses the outline). Confirmed link-behavior asymmetry: the two in-paragraph text links (Templates, Learning) have NO target and NO rel (same-tab navigation); the two CTA anchors (Deploy Now, Documentation) use target=_blank rel="noopener noreferrer". No layout shift/overflow observed; logo uses priority + fixed 100x20 dimensions.

SCREENSHOTS (qa-screenshots/): mobile-375x667.png, tablet-768x1024.png, desktop-1440x900.png (all light) and desktop-dark-1440x900.png (prefers-color-scheme: dark emulated; inverted logo, black bg confirming dark CSS vars + dark: utilities). Layout is centered single-column on mobile and left-aligned within max-w-3xl from the sm: breakpoint up.

ARTIFACTS: evidence/{build.log, lint.log, runtime.md, runtime.json, headers.log, README.md} and the four screenshots above. Temporary helper scripts and server logs were removed after use.

DEVIATIONS: used `next start` (production build) rather than `next dev` for the server-backed captures to avoid dev-overlay noise and because background processes are not shared across tool calls; the dev server was also confirmed to start and report Ready. Used playwright-core directly (equivalent to the playwright power) because the power's tool runs in a separate call where the local server would not be alive.
